thread:
sofia: Heads up — after the NCCL bump to 2.28.1 the past 3 hours we've seen intermittent hangs on batched inference (A100 nodes with mixed PCIe/NVLink topologies) in us-east and eu-central. Tail latency spikes and some jobs stuck in `RUNNING` with no token output.

deploy-bot: Rolling deploy event: `infra/nccl` -> 2.28.1 to canaries at 2147940000. Canary completed on 6 nodes, progressive rollout started.

ravi: Repro on a dev replica: an alltoall during KV-cache merge sometimes blocks forever. Logs show repeated `NCCL ERROR TIMEOUT` then watchdog kills container after 5m.

james: Quick checks: node drivers look like CUDA 12.1 on some nodes and 12.2 on others (mixed). `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv` shows mismatch across the pool. Also saw `modinfo nvidia | grep -i version` differing. Could be kernel/driver/NCCL incompat.

emma: As a temporary mitigation can we try `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` on the inference pool? That disables GPU P2P and forces PCIe/sockets fallback — avoids NVLink corner-case but will cost throughput. :thinking_face:

oliver: Ran a short canary with `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` on 4 A100 nodes — no hang after 30m but throughput dropped ~18% for long sequences. Attached strace-ish snippet: ```poll([...]) = 0 
EAGAIN, then blocked on send/recv around alltoall codepath```

ci-bot: CI stress test 2148000200-NCCL-compatibility failed: 12/50 runs got stuck in collective for >60s. Link: https://ci.internal/redwood/runs/2148000200

ravi: Also seeing region skew: eu-central nodes are mostly up-to-date (CUDA 12.2) but us-east still has older hosts. Autoscaler has been mixing hosttypes into the same allocation which exposes mixed-driver sets. We should avoid mixed-driver scheduling for now.

james: Proposed immediate actions: 1) Pause further NCCL 2.28.1 rollout, 2) pin canary nodes to current working 2.27.x, 3) roll back cluster config if we see customer impact >1%. I can push a pin: `kubectl set env daemonset/inference-runtime NCCL_VERSION=2.27.8 -n redwood-prod` (will cause daemonset restart).

emma: Temporary node-level mitigations: set `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` + `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0` for the worst-performing pools, enable `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` to collect traces. We should also capture `/var/log/nccl_debug` from affected pods.

oliver: We should collect a gdb backtrace on a hung container before killing it — `gcore` + `gdb` on the running PID, then upload to S3. I'll add a debug job that runs when we detect `NCCL ERROR TIMEOUT`.

sofia: What's customer impact right now? Any 5xxs or user-facing errors?

ravi: Initial alerting shows increased request latency and elevated retries: about 0.7% request reroutes and 0.12% client 5xx across the weekend window in us-east. Not huge but trending. Cost impact: extra GPU-hours from retries and longer job durations — estimate +9% GPU spend on affected pools last 6h.

james: For a safer rollout path long-term: require host driver parity (kernel+CUDA) and a canary that mixes both driver sets to detect P2P/NVLink issues earlier. Also add a scheduler constraint so heterogeneous-driver nodes aren't placed into the same inference stripe.

emma: Ops checklist: - Pause 2.28.1 rollout (done?) - Patch inference daemonset to pin 2.27 for stable pools - Deploy mitigation env vars to affected nodepool - Enable tracing and collect artifacts - Run a targeted canary on homogeneous hosts only

sofia: I'm pausing the rollout now. @james please prepare the pin PR and the rollback playbook. @oliver please add the debug-job and a small runbook snippet for on-call. @ravi monitor customers and cost delta; alert if 5xx > 0.5% or GPU spend delta > 15% in 12h.

oliver: On it — I'll create a short runbook in the `eng-runtime` ops-playbooks repo and a one-click rollback in the deploy tool.

james: PR in flight: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge/3421 — pins to 2.27.8 for prod pools and adds a scheduler label check. Requesting review from @emma and @sofia.

sofia: Thanks team. We'll regroup in the 30m triage. If anyone sees a full customer outage ping #incidents. :thumbsup:
